points: Your microphone audio goes to ElevenLabs, our voice provider, only while the conversation is open.
Audio is not recorded or kept. The text transcript is deleted after 30 days.
We don't send your name or any account details. Please don't share personal information.
The characters you talk with are AI. They can make mistakes, and nothing they say is policy.
Each conversation stops after 3 minutes. End it any time, or type instead of talking.

offer.headline: Have the conversation.
steps: Press Start and allow the microphone, or choose Type instead. {first} speaks first.
Talk the way you would at work, in your own words. There is no script.
When it is settled, say goodbye. What you agreed becomes your answer once you confirm it.

conversations.speaker: mgr_ortiz
conversations.title: Talk it through with Dana
conversations.pitch: Practice the real conversation. Dana is a live AI character who answers what you actually say. It takes about 2 minutes.
conversations.scene: Thursday morning. Priya logged 44 hours in week 1, and Dana never approved overtime. Her event budget is tight, and she wants the time card cut to 40. Three minutes with Dana. Settle what happens to those hours.

coaching.text: You named the rule: hours over 40 in a workweek are paid as overtime, approved or not.
Name the rule out loud next time: hours over 40 in a workweek are paid as overtime, approved or not.
You kept the hours in week 1: overtime is counted per workweek, so moving hours would make the record false.
You gave Dana the real fix: a conversation with Priya about getting approval first.
Give Dana the real fix: a conversation with Priya about getting approval first. The time card stays as worked.
Managers fix their own team's time. You advise and follow up; you don't edit it for them.
You kept it respectful. Managers come back to the HCM who helps them, not the one who corrects them.
Dana is your partner here. A respectful explanation lands better and keeps her coming back to you.

conversations.speaker: mgr_bell
conversations.title: Talk it through with Marcus
conversations.pitch: Practice the real conversation. Marcus is a live AI character who answers what you actually say, and he wants Noor started fast. It takes about 2 minutes.
conversations.scene: Monday morning. Noor just accepted Marcus's offer, her background check is still pending, and his team is short-handed for events this week. He wants her to start Wednesday and do the paperwork after. Three minutes with Marcus. Settle when Noor can start.

coaching.text: You held the gate: no one starts until PCB sends clear to start and you convert her.
Name the gate next time: no one starts until PCB sends clear to start and you convert her.
You kept the I-9 on time: Section 1 is due by her first day, so the paperwork can't come after.
Add the I-9 next time: Section 1 is due by her first day, so the paperwork can't come after.
You turned down unpaid shadowing: anything Noor does for the office is work, and work is paid.
You gave Marcus a plan he can work with, not just a no.
Give Marcus a date or a plan, so the no comes with a next step.
You kept it respectful. Managers come back to the HCM who helps them, not the one who corrects them.
Marcus is your partner here. A respectful explanation lands better and keeps him coming back to you.
